title: Extended-answer structure
examples: Should I write a plan before I start my essay?
How many paragraphs should I use for a big answer?
What makes a good conclusion for an essay?

explain.say: First you need to plan your entire answer carefully.
Next you write your main body paragraphs one by one.

items: Topic Sentence: Main point of the paragraph
Explanation: Linking evidence back to the question

explain.say: A good paragraph always has a clear main idea.
Finally you must write a strong conclusion to finish well.
For a real life example think about planning a trip.
The most common mistake is forgetting to link everything together.

faq.q: How long should my plan be for a big answer?
faq.a: Your plan should be detailed enough to guide your writing process. It needs to show you have thought about all parts of the question.
asks: Do I need to write down everything in my plan?
What is the purpose of planning an essay?

faq.q: What is the difference between evidence and explanation?
faq.a: Evidence is the fact you use to support your point. Explanation is you saying how that fact proves your point.
asks: Should I just list facts in my paragraphs?
Is explanation the same as analysis?

faq.q: Should I introduce new arguments in my conclusion?
faq.a: No you should not introduce new arguments in the conclusion. The conclusion is for wrapping up what you have already said.
asks: Can I add extra information at the end?
Is the conclusion a place for new ideas?

faq.q: If I use a lot of examples, do I need more paragraphs?
faq.a: Yes generally each new main idea or type of example needs its own dedicated paragraph. This keeps your answer clear and balanced.
asks: Does every example need a new paragraph?

faq.q: Is it okay if my conclusion is very short?
faq.a: It should be long enough to summarize your main arguments properly. A very short conclusion might leave the reader feeling unfinished.
asks: Can I just write one sentence for the conclusion?
How long should the conclusion be compared to the body?

facts: A plan helps organize your thoughts before writing begins.
Each body paragraph should focus on one main idea or point.
A good conclusion summarizes key points without introducing new evidence.
The structure Point, Evidence, Explanation is useful for body paragraphs.

quiz.say: If you are planning an essay on renewable energy, what is the best first step?
quiz.why: You must know exactly what the question asks before you can plan any points.

wrong.0: This is wrong because the conclusion depends on the points you make in the body.
wrong.1: This is wrong because you need a structure to organize those examples properly.
wrong.2: This is wrong because you need a full plan before you can write strong topic sentences.

quiz.say: In a body paragraph, what must you do after providing evidence?

options.show: Move to the next paragraph immediately
options.say: Move to the next paragraph immediately

options.show: Explain how the evidence supports your point
options.say: Explain how the evidence supports your point

quiz.why: Explanation is where you show the reader the connection between your fact and your main argument.

wrong.0: This is wrong because you must explain the evidence first to make the point clear.
wrong.1: This is wrong because you should explain the current evidence before adding more facts.
wrong.2: This is wrong because restating the topic sentence does not explain the evidence itself.

quiz.say: When writing a conclusion, what should you avoid doing?

options.show: Introducing any brand new arguments or facts
options.say: Introducing any brand new arguments or facts

quiz.why: The conclusion must wrap up what you have already discussed; new information confuses the reader.

wrong.0: This is wrong because a summary should be concise, not overly detailed.
wrong.2: This is wrong because simply repeating the question does not summarize your answer.
wrong.3: This is wrong because the conclusion should be clear and direct, not overly complicated.
